body: The McCormick County Council approved the rezoning for the Pollard data center project 3-2 on September 10, 2026, WRDW/WAGT reported. Pollard Land Company had sought the rezoning, and the county planning commission recommended denying it at a July 30 meeting. At the September meeting the council also voted 3-2 against a proposed nine-month pause on all data center development. Pollard representatives estimated the data center would take about six years to build and use 300,000 to 500,000 gallons of water a day, and a natural gas pipeline is planned nearby. Earlier WRDW reports described the rezoning request as covering about 1,000 acres; the station's report on the lawsuit describes a 678-acre data center.

A group of residents filed suit on November 6. According to WRDW, the complaint alleges that the county failed to follow required zoning procedures, did not adequately evaluate the project's effects on infrastructure and neighboring properties, approved a rezoning inconsistent with its comprehensive plan, and did not give the public required notice or an equal opportunity to comment. The complaint also cites a June 30 email stating that the local Commission of Public Works had sent Pollard Lumber a letter committing 1 million gallons of water per day.
WRDW reported that it asked the county, each council member and the residents' counsel for comment and had not received a reply as of publication. The report did not identify the court.

timeline.label: McCormick County Planning Commission recommends denying the Pollard rezoning
County council approves the rezoning 3-2 and rejects a nine-month data center pause 3-2
Residents sue the county, challenging the rezoning
